'''''Mazus pumilus''''', commonly called '''Japanese mazus''',<ref name=USDA>{{PLANTS|id=MAPU7|taxon=Mazus pumilus|accessdate=6 September 2018}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the [[Mazaceae]] family. It is native to south and east Asia, where it is found in [[Bhutan]], [[China]], [[India]], [[Pakistan]], [[Bangladesh]], [[Indonesia]], [[Japan]], [[Korea]], [[Nepal]], [[New Guinea]], the [[Philippines]], [[Russia]], [[Taiwan]], [[Thailand]], and [[Vietnam]].<ref name=FoC>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=210001250 ''Mazus pumilus''] Flora of China</ref> It is an [[invasive species]] in North America.<ref name=USDA/>

Its natural habitat is wet grasslands, streambanks, and trailsides.<ref name=FoC/> It is tolerant of disturbance, and can be found in areas such as cultivated fields, sidewalk cracks, and waste ground.<ref name=FoC/><ref>[http://had0.big.ous.ac.jp/plantsdic/angiospermae/dicotyledoneae/sympetalae/scrophulariaceae/tokiwahaze/tokiwahaze.htm ''Mazus pumilus''] (in Japanese), Okayama University Plant Ecology Laboratory</ref> It is a very common species in Japan.<ref name=Ohwi>{{cite book |last=Ohwi |first=Jisaburo |date=1965 |title=Flora of Japan |publisher=Smithsonian Institution |page=795}}</ref> 

It is an upright annual growing to 30 cm tall. Its flowers are purple and white with yellow spots on the throat. Flowers are produced throughout the growing season.<ref name=FoC/>
